record.title: The maximum G-different permutation conjecture
record.statement:
A **natural graph** is a simple graph whose vertex set is a finite subset of $\mathbb{N}$. Two infinite permutations of $\mathbb{N}$ are **$G$-different** if, for some coordinate $i\in\mathbb{N}$, the two entries at that coordinate are the endpoints of an edge of $G$. Let $\kappa(G)$ be the maximum cardinality of a set of infinite permutations that are pairwise $G$-different, and define

$$
K(\ell)=\max\{\kappa(G)\;\ |E(G)|=\ell\}.
$$

**The maximum G-different permutation conjecture.** For every $\ell\in\mathbb{N}$,

$$
K(\ell)=3^\ell.
$$

The paper proves that $K(\ell)$ lies between $3^\ell$ and $4^\ell$ for every natural number $\ell$, so the conjectured exact lower endpoint remains unresolved.
record.source_name: János Körner, Claudia Malvenuto and Gábor Simonyi, “Graph-different permutations”, arXiv:0709.4387 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.4387

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2007).

record.title: The product replacement graph connectivity conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, and let $d(G)$ denote the minimum size of a generating set of $G$. For an integer $k\geq d(G)$, let $\tilde \Gamma_k(G)$ be the extended product replacement algorithm graph whose vertices are the generating $k$-tuples of $G$ and whose edges correspond to Nielsen moves.

**Connectivity conjecture.** If $k\geq d(G)+1$, then $\tilde \Gamma_k(G)$ is connected.

This question was raised by Pak because no examples were known of a finite group $G$ and an integer $k\geq d(G)+1$ for which the extended product replacement graph is disconnected. The conjecture is known for finite abelian and finite solvable groups, and general bounds are known, but it is not established for all finite groups.
record.source_name: Shelly Garion, “Connectivity of the Product Replacement Algorithm Graph of PSL(2,q)”, arXiv:0712.1357 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0712.1357

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2007). “This conjecture has been proved only in the following cases.”

record.title: Conjecture on the cop number of graphs embedded in non-orientable surfaces
record.statement:
Let $c(g)$ denote the maximum cop number of a graph embedded in an orientable surface of genus $g$, and let $\tilde c(g)$ denote the corresponding maximum for graphs embedded in a non-orientable surface of genus $g$. **Surface cop-number conjecture.**

$$
\tilde c(g)=c(\lfloor g/2\rfloor).
$$

The preceding argument establishes the upper bound $\tilde c(g)\leq c(g-1)$ using the orientable double cover, while the equality for all genera is presented as a conjecture and its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Nancy E. Clarke, Samuel Fiorini, Gwenaël Joret and Dirk Oliver Theis, “A note on the Cops & Robber game on graphs embedded in non-orientable surfaces”, arXiv:0803.0538 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0803.0538

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2008).

record.title: Unbounded integral point sets over prime residue rings
record.statement:
For a prime $p$, let $\dot{\mathcal{I}}(\mathbb{Z}_p,2)$ denote the maximum cardinality of an integral point set in the plane over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ in general position. **Unboundedness conjecture.** For each positive integer $l$ there is a prime threshold $p'$ such that for all primes $p\ge p'$,

$$
\dot{\mathcal{I}}(\mathbb{Z}_p,2)\ge l.
$$

The surrounding discussion notes that several non-isomorphic sets attain the upper bound and suggests only the weaker observation that the value is at least $7$ for sufficiently large primes. Over the integers, the corresponding question for seven points is stated to remain unsolved.
record.source_name: Sascha Kurz, “Integral point sets over finite fields”, arXiv:0804.1289 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.1289

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2008).

record.title: Conjecture on the tightness of the two lower bounds for integral point sets over $\mathbb{Z}_n^2$
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{I}(n,2)$ denote the maximum number of points in an integral point set over $\mathbb{Z}_n^2$. The paper gives two lower bounds for this quantity, one in Lemma 1 and one in Lemma 2. **Tightness conjecture.** For all $n\in\mathbb{N}$, either the lower bound of Lemma 1 or the lower bound of Lemma 2 is tight. This conjecture asserts that one of the two stated constructions always attains the maximum; the source provides no evidence of a resolution.
record.source_name: Axel Kohnert and Sascha Kurz, “Integral point sets over Z_n^m”, arXiv:0804.1299 (2008).

record.title: The circle conjecture for plane integral point sets in semi-general position
record.statement:
A **plane integral point set** is a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane whose pairwise distances are integers; it is in **semi-general position** when no three points are collinear. A set has **minimum diameter** when its diameter is minimal among plane integral point sets of the same cardinality.

**Circle conjecture.** The points of a plane integral point set in semi-general position are situated on a circle.

The paper notes that all known examples in semi-general position with minimum diameter lie on a common circle, and proves this structure for sets with at most $36$ points. The conjecture asserts the circle property in general.
record.source_name: Sascha Kurz and Alfred Wassermann, “On the minimum diameter of plane integral point sets”, arXiv:0804.1307 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.1307

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2008).

record.title: The collinear-subset conjecture for minimum-diameter plane integral point sets
record.statement:
Let $n\ge 9$, and let a **plane integral point set with minimum diameter** be a plane integral point set of $n$ points whose diameter is minimal among such sets. A subset is **collinear** when all of its points lie on one line.

**Collinear-subset conjecture.** For $n\ge 9$, a plane integral point set with minimum diameter contains a subset of $n-1$ collinear points.

The paper proves this description for $9\le n\le 122$. The conjecture extends that computationally established range to all $n\ge 9$.
record.source_name: Sascha Kurz and Alfred Wassermann, “On the minimum diameter of plane integral point sets”, arXiv:0804.1307 (2008).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.1307

record.title: Sum-rate conjecture for the binary skew-symmetric broadcast channel
record.statement:
Let $(U,V)$ be auxiliary random variables and let $X,Y_1,Y_2$ be the input and outputs of the binary skew-symmetric channel with $p=\frac{1}{2}$, such that $(U,V) \to X \to (Y_1,Y_2)$ is a Markov chain. **Sum-rate conjecture.** The following inequality holds:

$$
I(U;Y_1) + I(V;Y_2) - I(U;V) \leq \max\{I(X;Y_1), I(X;Y_2)\}.
$$

If true, this conjecture would bound the sum rate of the Márton inner bound by approximately $0.3616$, while the evaluated outer bound has maximum sum rate approximately $0.3711$. Thus it would establish that the inner and outer bounds are not tight for the binary skew-symmetric channel.
record.source_name: Chandra Nair and Vincent Wang Zizhou, “On the inner and outer bounds for 2-receiver discrete memoryless broadcast channels”, arXiv:0804.3825 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.3825

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2008).

record.title: The subdivided complete-graph conjecture for the cop number
record.statement:
Let $K_n$ be a complete graph, and let $G$ be any graph obtained from $K_n$ by subdividing its edges, possibly a non-uniform number of times. The cop number of $G$, denoted by $\operatorname{cop}(G)$, is the minimum number of cops needed to capture a robber on $G$.

**Subdivided complete-graph conjecture.** For every such graph $G$,

$$
\operatorname{cop}(G)\in O(\sqrt n).
$$

This conjecture would imply Meyniel's conjecture that every graph on $n$ vertices has cop number in $O(\sqrt n)$. The surrounding discussion establishes an upper bound of at most $2$ for the uniformly subdivided complete graph considered in the construction, but does not resolve the conjecture for arbitrary subdivisions.
record.source_name: Gwenaël Joret, Marcin Kamiński and Dirk Oliver Theis, “The Cops and Robber game on graphs with forbidden (induced) subgraphs”, arXiv:0804.4145 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.4145

record.title: The algebraic Conforti–Cornuéjols conjecture on normality of the Rees algebra
record.statement: Let $\cal C$ be a clutter, let $\tau({\cal C}')$ and $\nu({\cal C}')$ denote the minimum vertex-cover and maximum matching sizes of a minor $\cal C'$, and let $R[It]$ be the Rees algebra of the edge ideal $I$. **Algebraic Conforti–Cornuéjols conjecture.** If $\tau({\cal C}')=\nu({\cal C}')$ for all minors $\cal C'$ of $\cal C$, then $R[It]$ is normal. This is stated as an algebraic version of the packing-property conjecture and is presented as unresolved in the source.
record.source_name: Alejandro Flores-Méndez, Isidoro Gitler and Enrique Reyes, “On 2-partitionable clutters and the MFMC property”, arXiv:0806.1772 (2008).

record.title: Non-recursive enumerability for effective graph models
record.statement:
Let $\mathscr{M}$ be an **effective graph model**, that is, a graph model satisfying the paper's effectiveness condition. Write $Th(\mathscr{M})$ for its equational theory.

**Effective graph-model conjecture.** All the effective graph models have non-r.e. equational theories.

This is stated as an open instance of the Scott-semantics conjecture, stronger than the claim about the minimum equational graph theory. The surrounding results establish non-r.e. order theories for all graph models, but not this equational-theory claim.
record.source_name: Chantal Berline, Giulio Manzonetto and Antonio Salibra, “Effective lambda-models vs recursively enumerable lambda-theories”, arXiv:0806.2264 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.2264

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2008). “Hence, the following instances of Conjecture are still open; we state them from the weaker to the stronger one.”

record.title: Domination conjecture for triangulations with finitely many non-six-valent vertices
record.statement: A **triangulation** is a plane graph in which every face, including the outer face, is bounded by a triangle. The degree of a vertex is its number of incident edges. **The bounded-exception domination conjecture.** For every constant $t$, there exists an integer $n_t$ such that every $n$-vertex triangulation with at most $t$ vertices whose degree is not $6$, and with $n\geq n_t$, has a dominating set of size at most $n/4$. This extends the paper's maximum-degree-six result to triangulations that are degree six except at a bounded number of vertices; the supplied text does not resolve it.
record.source_name: Erika L. C. King and Michael J. Pelsmajer, “Dominating Sets in Plane Triangulations”, arXiv:0806.2421 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.2421

record.title: Concentration conjecture for the verification decoder's edge-type counts
record.statement:
Let $t$ denote the discrete decoding time, let $R_{i,j,k}(t)$ be the number of edges connected to IVNs of type $r_{i,j,k}$, and let $\bar{R}_{i,j,k}(t)=E[R_{i,j,k}(t)\mid H_t]$, where $H_t$ is the history up to time $t$. Let $\alpha_0 n$ be the lifespan of the random process and let $d_v$ be the maximum variable-node degree. **Concentration conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty}\Pr\left(\sup_{0\le t\le \alpha_0 n}\left|\bar{R}_{i,j,k}(t)-R_{i,j,k}(t)\right|\ge n^{5/6}\right)=0
$$

for all $\{i,j,k:0\le i\le d_v,0\le j\le d_v,0\le k\le d_v,0\le i+j+k\le d_v\}$. This concentration is one of the unproved assumptions needed to establish the correctness of the decoding analysis.
record.source_name: Fan Zhang and Henry D. Pfister, “Analysis of Verification-based Decoding on the q-ary Symmetric Channel for Large q”, arXiv:0806.3243 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.3243

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2008).

record.title: The Ferrers-diagram rank-metric code dimension conjecture
record.statement: Let ${\cal F}$ be a Ferrers diagram and let $\delta$ be a positive integer. For each $i$ with $0\leq i\leq\delta-1$, let $\nu_i$ be the number of dots in ${\cal F}$ outside the first $i$ rows and the rightmost $\delta-1-i$ columns. The quantity $\min_i\{\nu_i\}$ is the upper bound for the dimension of a Ferrers-diagram rank-metric code with minimum rank distance $\delta$. **Ferrers-diagram rank-metric code dimension conjecture.** The upper bound of Theorem~ is attainable for any given set of parameters $q$, ${\cal F}$, and $\delta$. This conjecture asserts the existence of an optimal Ferrers-diagram rank-metric code for every Ferrers diagram and minimum rank distance; such codes would meet the general upper bound and are central to constructions of constant-dimension codes.
record.source_name: Tuvi Etzion and Natalia Silberstein, “Error-Correcting Codes in Projective Spaces via Rank-Metric Codes and Ferrers Diagrams”, arXiv:0807.4846 (2009).

record.title: Erdős–Hajnal conjecture for the extremal function $h_1^{(3)}$
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the minimal family of 3-uniform hypergraphs generated from the empty hypergraphs on $1$ and $2$ vertices and an edge by the operation $H(G,v)$. Let $g_1^{(3)}(s)$ be the maximum number of edges in a member of $\mathcal{F}$ with $s$ vertices, and let $h_1^{(3)}(s)$ be the transition value from the generalized Ramsey-function conjecture. **Erdős–Hajnal conjecture.** For every positive integer $s$,

$$
h_1^{(3)}(s)=g_1^{(3)}(s)+1.
$$

The source notes the already established inequality $h_1^{(3)}(s)>g_1^{(3)}(s)$ and conjectures that this lower bound is tight.
record.source_name: David Conlon, Jacob Fox and Benny Sudakov, “Hypergraph Ramsey numbers”, arXiv:0808.3760 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.3760

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2008).

record.title: Erdős–Hajnal equality conjecture for the functions $F_1$ and $g_1^{(3)}$
record.statement:
For a positive integer $s$, let $F_1(s)$ be the maximum number of triples $(a,b,c)$ with $1\leq a<b<c\leq s$ satisfying a prescribed three-coloring pattern on the edges $(a,b)$, $(b,c)$, and $(a,c)$, maximized over all edge-colorings of the complete graph on $[s]$ with colors $I$, $II$, and $III$. Let $g_1^{(3)}(s)$ be the maximum number of edges in a member of the recursively defined family $\mathcal{F}$ of 3-uniform hypergraphs on $s$ vertices. **Erdős–Hajnal equality conjecture.** For every positive integer $s$,

$$
F_1(s)=g_1^{(3)}(s).
$$

The source explains that this equality would imply $h_1^{(3)}(s)=F_1(s)+1=g_1^{(3)}(s)+1$, and hence the preceding Erdős–Hajnal conjecture; no resolution is given.
record.source_name: David Conlon, Jacob Fox and Benny Sudakov, “Hypergraph Ramsey numbers”, arXiv:0808.3760 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.3760

record.title: Alternative general global maximum conjecture for the rank-two likelihood model
record.statement:
Let $n\ge2$ and let $s,t$ satisfy $0<s\le t$. Let $L(P)$ be the likelihood function defined in the source by equation (newLP). **Alternative likelihood conjecture.** The matrix

$$
P=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{2s}{n^2(s+t)}&\frac1{n^2}&\cdots&\frac1{n^2}&\frac{2t}{n^2(s+t)}\\frac1{n^2}&\frac1{n^2}&\cdots&\frac1{n^2}&\frac1{n^2}\\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\vdots\\frac1{n^2}&\frac1{n^2}&\cdots&\frac1{n^2}&\frac1{n^2}\\frac{2t}{n^2(s+t)}&\frac1{n^2}&\cdots&\frac1{n^2}&\frac{2s}{n^2(s+t)}\end{pmatrix}
$$

is a global maximum for $L(P)$.

This is another proposed extension of the likelihood maximization result to arbitrary $n$. The supplied context does not define $L(P)$ or establish the claim, so its resolution is unclear.
record.source_name: Mingfu Zhu, Guangran Jiang and Shuhong Gao, “Solving the 100 Swiss Francs Problem”, arXiv:0809.4627 (2011).

record.title: The 1.25 speedup conjecture for unicasts and broadcasts
record.statement: Consider a $K\times N$ switch with traffic patterns consisting only of unicasts and broadcasts. **The 1.25 speedup conjecture.** The minimum speedup required to achieve $100\%$ throughput is exactly $1.25$. The paper presents this as a conjectural extension of the $2\times N$ enhanced-conflict-graph approach, motivated by simulations; whether the bound is exact for general $K$ and $N$ remains open.
record.source_name: MinJi Kim, Jay Kumar Sundararajan, Muriel Medard, Atilla Eryilmaz and Ralf Koetter, “Network Coding in a Multicast Switch”, arXiv:0810.1735 (2008).

record.title: Monotonicity and vanishing-minimum-energy conjecture for discrete cavity flow
record.statement:
Fix the boundary velocity $v$ and the discretization $N$. Let $F$ be the kinetic-energy objective, let $u_0(v,N)$ denote the solution at $R=0$, and let $E_{\min}(R,v,N)$ be the minimum kinetic energy among solutions of the discrete cavity flow problem at Reynolds number $R$.

**Minimum-energy conjecture.** For every $R\geq 0$,

$$
F(u_0(v,N))=E_{\min}(0,v,N)\geq E_{\min}(R,v,N)\geq 0,
$$

and

$$
E_{\min}(R,v,N)\longrightarrow 0\quad\text{as }R\longrightarrow\infty.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the numerical observation that the minimum energy decreases with $R$. The supplied text says that the vanishing of the minimum kinetic energy for increasing $R$ is left for future research; no resolution is given.
record.source_name: Martin Mevissen, Kosuke Yokoyama and Nobuki Takayama, “Solutions of Polynomial Systems Derived from the Steady Cavity Flow Problem”, arXiv:0811.2249 (2008).

record.title: Conjecture on the maximal degree of minimal generators of graph invariant rings
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{I}_n$ be the invariant ring associated with graphs on $n$ vertices, and let $\beta(\mathcal{I}_n)$ be the largest degree of an element in a minimal homogeneous generating set.

**Maximal-generator-degree conjecture.** For every $n\ge4$,

$$
\beta(\mathcal{I}_n)=\binom n2-1.
$$

The equality is established in the source for $n=4$ and $n=5$. The general case is presented as a conjecture and remains open.
record.source_name: Nicolas M. Thiéry, “Algebraic invariants of graphs; a study based on computer exploration”, arXiv:0812.3082 (2008).

record.title: Uniqueness conjecture for the minimizing parameter
record.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer, let $Q(\alpha,1)$ be the operator whose lowest eigenvalue is $\lambda_0(\alpha,1)$, and let $\hat{\nu}$ denote the minimum value of $\lambda_0(\alpha,1)$. A minimizing parameter is an $\alpha_{\rm min}\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfying $\lambda_0(\alpha_{\rm min},1)=\hat{\nu}$. **Uniqueness conjecture.** There exists a unique $\alpha_{\rm min}\in\mathbb{R}$ such that

$$
\lambda_0(\alpha_{\rm min},1)=\hat{\nu}.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by numerical computations. The source notes that uniqueness had been claimed for $k=1$ by Pan–Kwek and for arbitrary odd $k$ by Aramaki, but does not establish the claim or provide a resolution status.
record.source_name: Bernard Helffer and Yuri A. Kordyukov, “Semiclassical analysis of Schrödinger operators with magnetic wells”, arXiv:0812.5038 (2008).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.5038

record.title: Zhang's first conjecture on the phi invariant of polarized metrized graphs
record.statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be as above, let $CV(f)$ denote the set of singular fibers, and for $y\in CV(f)$ let $\Gamma_y$ be the polarized metrized graph of the fiber. Write $\delta_i(\Gamma_y)$ for the number of nodes of type $i$, where type $0$ means that partial normalization at the node is connected and type $i\geq1$ is determined by the minimum arithmetic genus of the two components. **Zhang's first conjecture.** There is a positive continuous function $c(\bar{g})$ of $\bar{g}\geq2$ such that, for every $y\in CV(f)$,

$$
\varphi(\Gamma_y)\geq c(\bar{g})\delta_0(\Gamma_y)+\sum_{i\geq1}\frac{2i(\bar{g}-i)}{\bar{g}}\delta_i(\Gamma_y).
$$

This inequality would imply the effective Bogomolov conjecture and hence the Bogomolov conjecture; the source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Zubeyir Cinkir, “Zhang's Conjecture and the Effective Bogomolov Conjecture over function fields”, arXiv:0901.3945 (2009).

record.title: Balanced blow-up conjecture for triangle densities
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with triangle density $\gamma$, and let $f_B(\gamma)$ denote the minimum possible density of copies of $B$ among such graphs. For an integer $t\geq 2$, set

$$
B=K_{t,t,t}.
$$

**Balanced blow-up conjecture.** For every $t\geq 2$,

$$
f_B(\gamma)=\gamma^{t^2}.
$$

This asserts that the random-graph upper bound has the correct order for balanced blowups of $K_3$. The supplied text does not state a resolution; it notes that improvements to the corresponding lower bound would have applications in theoretical computer science.
record.source_name: Asaf Shapira and Raphael Yuster, “On the Density of a Graph and its Blowup”, arXiv:0903.0198 (2009).

record.title: Alon-Saks-Seymour conjecture on biclique partitions
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $k$. A **biclique partition** is a partition of the edge set $E(G)$ into complete bipartite graphs.

**Alon-Saks-Seymour conjecture.** The minimum number of bicliques in such a partition is $k-1$.

This conjecture generalizes the Graham-Pollak theorem from complete graphs to arbitrary graphs of chromatic number $k$. Every graph has a partition of size $k-1$ obtained from a proper $k$-coloring, while the conjecture asserts that no smaller partition exists. The paper notes that only the folklore lower bound $\log_2 k$ was known at the time, and proves a superlogarithmic lower bound.
record.source_name: Dhruv Mubayi and Sundar Vishwanathan, “Biclique Coverings and the Chromatic Number”, arXiv:0903.3048 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0903.3048

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2009).

record.title: Conjecture on disjoint duplexes in Latin squares
record.statement:
A **$k$-plex** in a Latin square of order $n$ is a set of entries containing each row, column, and symbol exactly $k$ times. A **duplex** is a $2$-plex, and a **$k$-partition** is a partition of the Latin square into disjoint $k$-plexes.

**Duplex partition conjecture.** Every Latin square has the maximum possible number of disjoint duplexes. In particular, every Latin square of even order has a $2$-partition, and every Latin square of odd order has a $(2,2,2,\dots,2,1)$-partition.

The conjecture strengthens Ryser's conjecture and implies the existence of $k$-plexes for every even $k$ up to the order of the square. It is known for Latin squares of orders at most $8$ and for soluble groups, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Ian M. Wanless, “Transversals in Latin Squares”, arXiv:0903.5142 (2009).

record.title: The spectral gap conjecture for multi-species ASEP
record.statement:
Let $m=(m_1,\,\ldots,m_n)\in\mathcal M$ be a sector, let ${\rm Spec}(m)$ denote the spectrum in that sector, and let $E_j^{\pm}(m)=E^{\pm}(m_1+\cdots+m_j,m_{j+1}+\cdots+m_n)$ for $1\leq j\leq n-1$, where $E^{\pm}$ are the second largest eigenvalues in the corresponding one-species sectors. **Spectral gap conjecture.** In any sector $m=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)\in\mathcal M$, there is no eigenvalue $E\in{\rm Spec}(m)$ such that

$$
\max\{{\rm Re}\,E^{\pm}_1(m),\ldots,{\rm Re}\,E^{\pm}_{n-1}(m)\}< {\rm Re}\,E<0.
$$

The one-species case $n=2$ is immediate from the definition, and the conjecture had been checked in all sectors with $\dim V(m)<8000$; its general validity remains open.
record.source_name: Chikashi Arita, Atsuo Kuniba, Kazumitsu Sakai and Tsuyoshi Sawabe, “Spectrum in multi-species asymmetric simple exclusion process on a ring”, arXiv:0904.1481 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0904.1481

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2009).

record.title: Finite-translate perfect-squares conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\textsc{Squares}$ denote the set of perfect squares in $\mathbb Z$. **Finite-translate perfect-squares conjecture.** There exists a positive integer $k$ such that there are no sets $X,Y\subset\mathbb Z$ with $|X|=|Y|=k$ satisfying

$$
x+y\in\textsc{Squares}\quad\text{for all }x\in X\text{ and }y\in Y.
$$

This asks whether the maximum number of translates of a fixed-size set of integers into the perfect squares is finite for some size. Such a bound would have consequences for sum-product exponents on sparse graphs; the problem is stated as open.
record.source_name: Noga Alon, Omer Angel, Itai Benjamini and Eyal Lubetzky, “Sums and products along sparse graphs”, arXiv:0905.0135 (2009).

record.title: Rational generating-function conjecture for maximum independent sets of de Bruijn graphs
record.statement:
For a positive integer $d$ and a fixed diameter $D$, let $B(d,D)$ be the de Bruijn graph and let $a_{d,D}$ denote the number of maximum independent sets of $B(d,D)$. Consider its exponential generating function

$$
\sum_{d=1}^{\infty}\frac{a_{d,D}t^d}{d!}.
$$

**Rational generating-function conjecture.** If $D$ is a fixed odd prime number, then this exponential generating function is the ratio of two polynomials, each of degree $D-1$.
For $D=3$, the paper proves the analogous assertion with numerator and denominator of degree at most $2$; the conjecture proposes the stated degree bound for every fixed odd prime diameter.
record.source_name: Dustin A. Cartwright, Maria Angelica Cueto and Enrique A. Tobis, “The maximum independent sets of de Bruijn graphs of diameter 3”, arXiv:0905.3820 (2010).
record.references:

record.title: The arbitrary-target distribution conjecture for pebbling
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let $t$ be a positive integer. Define $\pi(G,t)$ to be the smallest number of pebbles such that every target distribution of size $t$ is reachable from every distribution of at least that size, and let $\pi_t(G)$ be the $t$-pebbling number.

**Arbitrary-target distribution conjecture.**

$$
\pi(G,t)=\pi_t(G).
$$

The source explains that reaching $t$ pebbles on any single vertex implies the inequality $\pi_t(G)\leq\pi(G,t)$ and conjectures the converse for arbitrary target distributions. The source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: David S. Herscovici, Benjamin D. Hester and Glenn H. Hurlbert, “t-Pebbling and Extensions”, arXiv:0905.3949 (2011).

record.title: Rectified Füredi–Mubayi signed domination conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices, minimum degree $\delta$, and signed domination number $\gamma_s(G)$. **Rectified signed domination conjecture.** There are constants $C$ and $\alpha$ satisfying $C\le 10$ and $0.18\le\alpha<0.21$ such that

$$
\gamma_s(G)\le\min\left\{{n\over\delta^\alpha},{Cn\over\sqrt\delta}\right\}.
$$

This rectifies the earlier Füredi–Mubayi conjecture by incorporating a separate bound for relatively small minimum degree; the source notes that the Petersen graph shows the constant in the original conjecture must satisfy $C>1$.
record.source_name: A. Poghosyan and V. Zverovich, “Discrepancy and Signed Domination in Graphs and Hypergraphs”, arXiv:0906.3993 (2009).

record.title: Continuous Hirsch conjecture
record.statement:
For a polytope $P$ of dimension $d$ defined by $n$ inequalities and a linear objective function $c$, let $\lambda_c(P)$ be the total curvature of its central path. Let $\Lambda(n,d)$ be the largest such total curvature over all such $P$ and $c$. **Continuous Hirsch conjecture.** There is a constant $K$ such that

$$
\Lambda(n,d)\leq Kn
$$

for all $n$ and $d$, equivalently $\Lambda(n,d)\in O(n)$. The previously proposed constant and linear-in-dimension bounds for central-path curvature were disproved by constructions showing exponential growth in $d$ and, for fixed $d\geq 2$, $\liminf_{n\to\infty}\Lambda(n,d)/n\geq\pi$.
record.source_name: Edward D. Kim and Francisco Santos, “An update on the Hirsch conjecture”, arXiv:0907.1186 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.1186

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2009). “Besides its implications in linear programming, which motivated the conjecture in the first place, it is one of the most fundamental open questions in polytope theory.”

record.title: Robertson's Hadwiger-type conjecture for degree sequences
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a graphic degree sequence, and let $\mathcal{R}(D)$ be the set of its simple graph realizations. Define $\chi(D)$ as the maximum chromatic number over graphs in $\mathcal{R}(D)$, and define $H(D)$ as the maximum order of a clique minor over graphs in $\mathcal{R}(D)$. **Robertson's conjecture.** For every graphic degree sequence $D$,

$$
\chi(D)\le H(D).
$$

This is a relaxation of Hadwiger's conjecture, which asks whether every graph of chromatic number $k$ contains a $k$-clique minor. The source states that Hadwiger's conjecture remains open, while this degree-sequence relaxation is presented as a conjecture; the paper's abstract says that it is settled, but the supplied candidate does not specify the proof status of this particular claim.
record.source_name: Zdenek Dvorak and Bojan Mohar, “Chromatic number and complete graph substructures for degree sequences”, arXiv:0907.1583 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.1583

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2009). “Despite many attempts, the Hadwiger Conjecture remains open, thus its relaxations are of high interest.”

record.title: Evenness conjecture for the trivializing number of virtual shadows
record.statement:
Let $S$ be a virtual shadow, namely a diagram with classical precrossings and virtual crossings, and let $\text{tr}(S)$ be its trivializing number: the minimum number of precrossings that must be resolved as virtual to guarantee that every resolution of the remaining precrossings is the unknot.

**Evenness conjecture.** For every virtual shadow $S$, $\text{tr}(S)$ is even.

This is proposed as an extension of the preceding result on virtual shadows. The source supplies no proof or evidence resolving the conjecture.
record.source_name: Allison Henrich, Noel MacNaughton, Sneha Narayan, Oliver Pechenik and Jennifer Townsend, “Classical and Virtual Pseudodiagram Theory and New Bounds on Unknotting Numbers and Genus”, arXiv:0908.1981 (2010).

record.title: Prime-depleted Szpiro conjecture for elliptic curves
record.statement:
Let $K$ be a number field. For an integral ideal $\mathfrak{D}=\prod_i\mathfrak{p}_i^{e_i}$, let $\sigma_J(\mathfrak{D})$ be the minimum of the Szpiro ratios obtained after removing up to $J$ of its prime-power factors. In particular, $\mathfrak{D}(E/K)$ denotes the discriminant ideal of an elliptic curve $E/K$.

**Prime-depleted Szpiro conjecture.** There exist an integer $J\ge0$ and a constant $C_3$, depending only on $K$, such that for all elliptic curves $E/K$,

$$
\sigma_J\bigl(\mathfrak{D}(E/K)\bigr)\le C_3.
$$

This weakens the classical Szpiro conjecture because increasing $J$ can only decrease the depleted Szpiro ratio. The paper introduces this conjecture as the key hypothesis used to obtain Lang's height conjecture.
record.source_name: Joseph H. Silverman, “Lang's Height Conjecture and Szpiro's Conjecture”, arXiv:0908.3895 (2009).

record.title: The $(q,t)$-deformed hook product formula for connected $d$-complete posets
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a connected $d$-complete poset with maximum element $v_0$, rank function $r:P\to\mathbb{N}$, top tree $T$, and $d$-complete coloring $c:P\to T$. For a $P$-partition $\sigma\in\mathcal{A}(P)$, let $W_P(\sigma;q,t)$ be the weight defined above, and let $\boldsymbol{z}^\sigma$ and $\boldsymbol{z}[H_P(v)]$ use the notation introduced in the paper. **The $(q,t)$-deformed hook product formula.** For every connected $d$-complete poset $P$,

$$
\sum_{\sigma\in\mathcal{A}(P)}W_P(\sigma;q,t)\boldsymbol{z}^\sigma=\prod_{v\in P}F(\boldsymbol{z}[H_P(v)];q,t).
$$

This is proposed as a $(q,t)$-deformation of the Peterson--Proctor hook formula. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been proved or disproved.
record.source_name: Soichi Okada, “(q,t)-deformations of multivariate hook product formulae”, arXiv:0909.0086 (2010).

record.title: Chudnovsky–Seymour–Sullivan conjecture on cycles in triangle-free digraphs
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple digraph with no directed cycle of length at most three; call such a digraph **3-free**. Let $\beta(G)$ be the minimum cardinality of a set $X\subseteq E(G)$ such that $G\setminus X$ is acyclic, and let $gamma(G)$ be the number of unordered pairs of nonadjacent vertices of $G$.

**Chudnovsky–Seymour–Sullivan conjecture.** If $G$ is a 3-free digraph, then

$$
\beta(G) \leq \frac{1}{2}\gamma(G).
$$

Chudnovsky, Seymour, and Sullivan proved the weaker bound $\beta(G)\leq\gamma(G)$, later improved by Dunkum, Hamburger, and Pór to $\beta(G)\leq 0.88\gamma(G)$; the conjectured factor $1/2$ remains unresolved in the source.
record.source_name: Kevin Chen, Sean Karson, Dan Liu and Jian Shen, “On the Chudnovsky-Seymour-Sullivan Conjecture on Cycles in Triangle-free Digraphs”, arXiv:0909.2468 (2009).
record.references:

record.title: The conjectured sharp threshold for connectivity and Hamiltonicity in random intersection graphs
record.statement:
Let $\alpha<1$, let

$$
p=\frac{\ln n+\omega}{m},
$$

and suppose that $\omega\to\infty$. Then, with high probability, the random intersection graph $\mathcal{G}(n,m,p)$ is $k$-connected for any constant $k$ and contains a Hamilton cycle.

**Connectivity and Hamiltonicity conjecture.** Under these assumptions, $\mathcal{G}(n,m,p)$ is $k$-connected for every fixed constant $k$ and contains a Hamilton cycle with high probability.

The conjecture is motivated by the minimum-degree phenomenon and proposes a tightening of the threshold function in the cited theorem for the case $\alpha<1$. The supplied text gives no resolution of this conjecture.
record.source_name: Katarzyna Rybarczyk, “Sharp threshold functions for the random intersection graph via coupling method?”, arXiv:0910.0749 (2009).

record.title: Core semisparsity conjecture for quotient representations of polytopes
record.statement:
Let $W$ be a group and let $N$ be a subgroup of $W$. The subgroup $N$ is **semisparse** in $W$ if it satisfies the semisparsity condition for quotient representations, and let $\operatorname{Core}(W,N)$ denote the core of $N$ in $W$, namely the largest normal subgroup of $W$ contained in $N$.

**Core semisparsity conjecture.** If $N$ is semisparse in $W$, then $\operatorname{Core}(W,N)$ is also semisparse.

A positive answer would imply that the two open questions described in the paper have negative answers: every finite polytope would have a well-defined quotient construction using the core, and every finite polytope would admit a presentation as a quotient of a finite regular polytope. The source does not report a resolution of this conjecture.

record.title: Vertex bound for regular minimal graphs
record.statement:
Let $d\geq 3$, let $n$ be the number of attaching points, and let $f_3(n)$ denote the comparison bound used in the paper for $3$-regular minimal graphs. A **$d$-regular minimal graph** is a minimal graph in which every vertex has degree $d$.

**Vertex-bound conjecture.** For all $d \geq 3$, the number of vertices of a $d$-regular minimal graph attached to $n$ points is

$$
\leq f_3(n).
$$

This conjecture asserts that $3$-regular minimal graphs provide the largest vertex count among regular minimal graphs with the same number of attaching points. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture is resolved.
record.source_name: Yashar Memarian, “On the Maximum Number of Vertices of Critically Embedded Graphs”, arXiv:0910.2469 (2015).

record.title: Half-degree conjecture for complementary tuples in balanced multipartite hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $H$) be an $n$-balanced $r$-partite $r$-graph, and let $I$ be a subset of $[r]:=\{1,2,\ldots,r\}$. An **$I$-tuple** is an element of $\times_{i\in I}V_i$, and write $I^c:=[r]\setminus I$. For an $I$-tuple $f$ and an $I^c$-tuple $g$, let $d(f)$ and $d(g)$ denote their degrees in $H$. **Half-degree conjecture.** If

$$
d(f)>\frac{n^{r-|I|}}{2}
$$

for every $I$-tuple $f$ and

$$
d(g)\geq\frac{n^{|I|}}{2}
$$

for every $I^c$-tuple $g$, then $H$ has a perfect matching. Thus, each tuple has degree at least roughly half of its possible degree, with a strict inequality on the $I$-side. The condition would weaken the sharp minimum-degree hypothesis proved earlier in the paper; its general validity is presented as an open problem.
record.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Agelos Georgakopoulos and Philipp Sprüssel, “Perfect matchings in r-partite r-graphs”, arXiv:0911.4008 (2009).

record.title: The superlinear blocker conjecture with bounded collinearities
record.statement:
For fixed $\ell$, let $b_\ell(n)$ be the minimum integer such that every set of $n$ points in the plane with no $\ell$ collinear points can be blocked by a set of $b_\ell(n)$ points. **Bounded-collinearity blocker conjecture.** For all fixed $\ell$,

$$
\frac{b_\ell(n)}{n}\rightarrow\infty\quad\text{as }n\rightarrow\infty.
$$

This generalizes the general-position case $b_3(n)=b(n)$ and is stated in the source as implying the Big-Line-Big-Chromatic-Number Conjecture; its general status remains open.
record.source_name: Attila Pór and David R. Wood, “On Visibility and Blockers”, arXiv:0912.1150 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.1150

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2009). “BigClique} is true for $k\leq 5$ or $\ell\leq3$ , and is open for $k=6$ or $\ell=4$.”

record.title: Conjecture that random graphs of fixed genus are asymptotically almost surely 4-chromatic
record.statement:
Let $g$ be fixed, and let $G_n$ be a graph chosen uniformly at random from the graphs of genus $g$ with $n$ vertices. The chromatic number of $G_n$ is the minimum number of colors needed to color its vertices so that adjacent vertices receive different colors.

**Chromatic-number conjecture.** The chromatic number of a random graph of fixed genus $g$ with $n$ vertices is asymptotically almost surely equal to $4$.

The preceding theorem establishes that the chromatic number is asymptotically almost surely either $4$ or $5$; the conjecture asserts that the value $4$ occurs with probability tending to $1$.
record.source_name: Guillaume Chapuy, Eric Fusy, Omer Gimenez, Bojan Mohar and Marc Noy, “Asymptotic enumeration and limit laws for graphs of fixed genus”, arXiv:1001.3628 (2010).

record.title: Superlinear blocker-number conjecture
record.statement:
Let $b(n)$ be the minimum integer such that some set of $n$ points in the plane in general position is blocked by a set of $b(n)$ points. **Superlinear blocker-number conjecture.**

$$
\frac{b(n)}{n}\rightarrow\infty\quad\text{as }n\rightarrow\infty.
$$

Known lower bounds are linear, including $b(n)\geq 2n-3$ and $b(n)\geq(\frac{25}{8}-o(1))n$; the conjecture that $b(n)$ is super-linear remains open.

record.title: The complete extremal-family conjecture for maximal-chain traces
record.statement:
Let $W(n,k,r)$ denote the maximum size of a family $\mathcal{A}\subset [n]^{(k)}$ whose trace on every $r$-subset of $[n]$ contains no maximal chain. **The complete extremal-family conjecture.** For $r\geq 2$, if $k+r-1\leq n<2k$, then

$$
W(n,k,r)=\binom{k+r-1}{k},
$$

and the only extremal family is of the form $[k+r-1]^{(k)}$; if $n>2k$, then

$$
W(n,k,r)=\binom{n-k+r-1}{r-1},
$$

and the only extremal family is of the form $\{A\in[n]^{(k)}:1,2,\ldots,k-r+1\in A\}$. This proposes the extremal numbers and equality cases for all indicated ranges of $n$, complementing the large-$n$ results proved earlier in the paper; the source supplies no resolution status for the full assertion.

record.title: The conjecture that the maximum Frobenius discrepancy for three generators is 14
record.statement:
Let $g_i(X)$ denote the relevant Frobenius-number discrepancy quantity for a set $X$ of generators, and let $f(3)$ be the corresponding maximum discrepancy over sets of cardinality three. The example

$$
g_{14}(8,9,15)=172,
$$

$$
g_{15}(8,9,15)=169
$$

shows that $f(3)\leq 14$.

**Frobenius discrepancy conjecture for three generators.**

$$
f(3)=14.
$$

The paper states that the value of $f(3)$ is not known; the displayed example supplies only the upper bound, so the equality remains open.

record.title: Symmetry of the algorithmic shuffling weight function
record.statement: Let $\varphi$ be the shuffling weight function produced by the algorithm, and call a shuffling weight function **symmetric** if $\varphi(i)+\varphi(31-i)$ is independent of $i$. **Symmetry conjecture.** The shuffling weight function produced by the algorithm is symmetric. The preceding examples exhibit this symmetry, but the statement is presented without a proof or resolution in the supplied text.

record.title: Meta-isomorphism conjecture for assembly maps
record.statement:
Fix a group $G$, a family of subgroups $\mathcal{F}$, and a $G$-homology theory $\mathcal{H}^G_*$. Let $E_{\mathcal{F}}(G)$ be the classifying $G$-space for the family $\mathcal{F}$, and let

$$
A_{\mathcal{F}}\colon\mathcal{H}^G_n(E_{\mathcal{F}}(G))\to\mathcal{H}^G_n(\operatorname{pt})
$$

be the assembly map induced by the projection $E_{\mathcal{F}}(G)\to\operatorname{pt}$.

**Meta-isomorphism conjecture.** The assembly map $A_{\mathcal{F}}$ is an isomorphism for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}$.

The source notes that the assertion is automatic for the family of all subgroups; the content is to choose the smallest possible family for which it remains true. Farrell–Jones and Baum–Connes conjectures are presented as instances.

record.title: Cantrell-Cosner-Lou concentration conjecture for positive local maxima
record.statement:
Let $u$ be the unique positive steady-state of the ecological model under (H1), where $m(x)\in C^{3}(\overline{\Omega})$ and is positive somewhere. The parameter $\alpha$ denotes the large advection parameter.

**Cantrell-Cosner-Lou concentration conjecture.** $u$ concentrates precisely on the set of positive local maximum points of $m(x)$ as $\alpha\rightarrow\infty$.

This conjecture concerns the concentration profile of the steady-state population as advection becomes large, refining known results that the total population tends to zero when the critical-point set of $m$ has Lebesgue measure zero and that, in one dimension under suitable finiteness assumptions, $u$ tends uniformly to zero away from critical points. The supplied text gives no resolution status for the conjecture.

record.title: The maximum-degree conjecture for extreme points of the Held–Karp relaxation
record.statement:
Consider extreme points of the Held–Karp relaxation on $n$ vertices, and let the maximum degree of an extreme point mean the maximum degree of its support graph. **The maximum-degree conjecture.** The maximum degree of extreme points on $n$ vertices is exactly

$$
\left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

The paper derives examples with large support degree and presents this claim as a conjecture based on enumeration through 12 vertices; whether the upper bound holds in general remains open.

record.title: Non-finite generation conjecture for the cohomology of Johnson filtration subgroups
record.statement:
Let $F_n$ be the free group of rank $n$, let $\Gamma^{s+1}$ be the $(s+1)$st term of its lower central series, and let $J_n^s$ denote the kernel of the homomorphism

$$
\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)\to \operatorname{Aut}(F_n/\Gamma^{s+1}).
$$

For integers $n$, $s$, and $i$ satisfying $3\leq n$, $2\leq s$, and $1\leq i\leq n-2$, **the authors' weak conjecture.** The cohomology group $H^i(J_n^s)$ is not finitely generated.

The preceding results give rapidly growing ranks for related cohomology groups and construct classes in the indicated degrees, but do not establish finite-generation failure for all these parameters. The conjecture remains open in the source.
